facts.fact: Hespress, citing unnamed informed sources, reports that communal tax officials issue annual orders de recettes (bills) for local taxes in GIR-CT and, in a next phase, recovery of those orders is to run through the same system, sent electronically to the Treasury accountants; payments are collected by the accountants, not recorded in the commune's system.

The Local Finance Directorate of the Interior Ministry's DGCT instructed prefecture and province services to have the collectivities' authorising officers use GIR-CT exclusively to upload revenue orders, and to abandon software the collectivities had bought or built; the orders pass electronically to the Treasury's accountants.

The report says the ministry, with the Treasury (TGR), has worked to generalise GIR-CT and to integrate the revenue offices of local public services, notably wholesale markets and slaughterhouses, but gives no count or share of collectivities using it.

GIR-CT is run by the Interior Ministry's DGCT in partnership with the Treasury (TGR); the instruction to use it exclusively was issued under central administration directives and circular D/2755/DFCT/2024 (budgets for 2025).

Instructions from the DGCT, reported on 29 May 2025, require exclusive use of GIR-CT and abandonment of earlier council software; the same report says taxpayers are urged to declare and pay local taxes through the e-platform set up with the Treasury.
